quiz_name: Quiz 4: Connected Signals, Scene Transitions, and Audio Streams! 📡🎵

questions.q: What is a Signal in the Godot Engine architecture?
opts: An event trigger sent by a node to communicate with code immediately when an action occurs
questions.exp: Signals are internal notification networks that tell scripts immediately when buttons are pressed, timers tick, or bodies collide!

questions.q: Which default signal is emitted by the Button node when a player clicks it?
questions.exp: The pressed() signal is fired by buttons immediately when a mouse click or finger tap is fully pressed and released!

questions.q: Which code command switches the current active scene in Godot (e.g. from Menu to Gameplay)?
questions.exp: We switch scenes in scripts using get_tree().change_scene() by providing the path to our target Scene template (.tscn)!

questions.q: Which command closes and shuts down the game application immediately?
questions.exp: The command get_tree().quit() requests the OS to shut down and close our game client peacefully and cleanly!

questions.q: What are sound effects (SFX) in video games?
opts: Short, interactive sound prompts triggered by specific events like jumps, strikes, or points
questions.exp: Sound Effects (SFX) are quick sound triggers activated by actions like coin collecting, bounces, or level completions!

questions.q: What is background music (BGM) in games?
opts: Continuous, looping musical tracks that set the atmospheric mood and tone of levels
questions.exp: Background Music (BGM) plays looping musical tracks continuously, keeping players relaxed or excited during gameplay!

questions.q: Which node is responsible for loading and playing audio streams inside Godot levels?
questions.exp: The AudioStreamPlayer2D node is our magical loudspeaker, playing audio files, sounds, and musical tracks!

questions.q: Which property in the AudioStreamPlayer2D holds the actual audio file (.mp3 or .wav)?
questions.exp: The 'Stream' property holds the sound resource file, telling the player which file to execute when triggered!

questions.q: Which command triggers the AudioStreamPlayer2D node to play its loaded audio stream?
questions.exp: We invoke the play() function on our audio nodes to start playing sound streams from the beginning!

questions.q: How can we stop the music or mute sounds when players request a pause in code?
opts: By calling the stop() function on our audio players
questions.exp: Invoking the stop() method immediately halts playback on the player node, muting its stream instantly!
